title: Sunset glow in Orion
caption: The reflection nebula NGC 2023 in Orion, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: NGC 2023 · constellation Orion · about 1500 light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: ESA/Hubble Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: Soft sunset shades wash across this scene of billowing gas, with a few odd greenish clumps tucked into the waves. It is the southern part of NGC 2023, a reflection nebula in Orion lying nearly 1,500 light-years from Earth, not far from the Flame and Horsehead Nebulae.

The nebula glows because of a massive young B-type star, a hot, blue-white kind of star several times hotter than the Sun. Its light makes the nebula unusually bright. The star sits just outside the frame at the upper left, and the bright flare along the left side is its light scattered inside Hubble's optics, not part of the nebula.

Stars are still forming here. Astronomers think the greenish clumps are Herbig–Haro objects: patches where gas shot out of newborn stars at hundreds of kilometres per second slams into surrounding material and makes it glow. Such features usually fade within a few thousand years.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (3.30 x 3.24 arcminutes) and distance (1500 light years), the frame spans roughly 1.4 × 1.4 light-years. Its light set out about 1,500 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys took this image: a blue filter (F475W) is shown as blue, a yellow filter (F625W) as green, and a near-infrared filter (F850LP) as red.
understand.eye: The red channel records near-infrared light the eye cannot see, and total exposures of 800 to 1200 seconds per filter gather far more light than the eye could.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: The whole of NGC 2023 is about four light-years across, and its waves of gas are 5000 times denser than the interstellar medium. The field of view of this image is 3.2 arcminutes.
alt: Billowing waves of gas in sunset-like shades with unusual greenish clumps, and a bright flare along the left side.
